clue.text: Approximate amount of time that's not processed internally

parts.note: an approximate figure is a rough one
an age is a long stretch of time

explanation.surface: Someone estimates a period that hasn't been worked through internally.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a description of dietary fibre, which passes through the gut undigested.
explanation.definitionFit: Dietary fibre is food material the body does not digest, passing through the gut unbroken.

clue.text: Capital city's un-Daliesque side?

definitions.note: a side is a sports team, here a football club

parts.note: Dali was a surrealist, so something not like his work is merely real
Madrid is the capital city of Spain

explanation.surface: A question about which part of the Spanish capital is not surreal.
explanation.walkthrough: Salvador Dali, the Spanish surrealist, gives the joke: the opposite of surreal is real.
explanation.definitionFit: A famous Spanish football club, and a side in sport is a team.

clue.text: Certain difference in Danube and Nile

indicators.note: a difference in the letters means they are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A geographer states a sure distinction between two great rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond denial is sure, so the word is a synonym of certain.

clue.text: World Cup hero injured, striker's head getting bandaged

indicators.note: a bandage wraps round, so one piece is wrapped inside the other

parts.note: injured means hurt

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A footballer hero is hurt and the striker has his head strapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoff Hurst scored a hat-trick for England in the 1966 World Cup final.
explanation.definitionFit: Geoff Hurst scored three goals when England won football's World Cup in 1966.

clue.text: Make climbing trees difficult for mechanic

definitions.meaning: read literally, smear grease so an ape cannot climb up
slang for someone who repairs engines, garage worker

explanation.surface: Advice on hindering tree-climbing, oddly offered for a garage worker.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is a whimsical cryptic reading: grease (the trees) for a monkey, so it slides off.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang term for a car repairer, from the oily state of the work.

clue.text: Fruit jam

definitions.meaning: a gourd such as a pumpkin or marrow, botanically a fruit
to jam is to crush or cram together

explanation.definitionFit: A gourd is botanically a fruit, and to crush or cram is to jam.

clue.text: "Clever" ahead of "stupid" initially, with sucker

indicators.note: one piece is placed in front of the next

parts.note: a quick mind is a clever one

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter

parts.note: and means with, joining

explanation.surface: A list of contrasting labels, clever before stupid, plus a sucker.
explanation.definitionFit: Wet sand that drags down and swallows whatever falls in, so it sucks things under.

clue.text: Topless mad host

indicators.note: topless means the first letter, its top in a down answer, is cut off

parts.note: barmy is British slang for mad

explanation.surface: A crazed party host without a shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: A host can mean a great multitude, such as a large body of soldiers.

clue.text: Drink for some horse

definitions.meaning: a German white wine from the Rhine
part of a horse, the joint in its hind leg

explanation.definitionFit: A Rhine white wine, and the joint halfway up a horse's hind leg.

clue.text: See 10
Order magnified with carbs?

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so these letters are put in a fresh sequence

explanation.surface: A supersized fast-food order with extra chips and bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both anagram and definition: a big burger meal is a magnified order, carbohydrates included.
explanation.definitionFit: A burger-and-chips meal from a fast-food chain is a carb-heavy order.

clue.text: Breeding expert in decline

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a decline is a reduction
a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: An authority on animal breeding is losing ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Breeding is the producing of offspring, the biological process of multiplying.

clue.text: Little and pale, say, dish of meat

parts.note: minute means very small

indicators.note: say signals a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a pale is a fence post, a stake

explanation.surface: A small, wan portion of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale' looks like a colour but is the noun meaning a wooden post.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin cut of beef cooked very quickly, a meal served on a plate.

clue.text: Second cut for game

parts.note: to second a motion is to back it
gammon is a cut of cured pork from the hind leg

explanation.surface: A second slice served up as game meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' tempts as meat after 'cut', but it is a board game; GAMMON is a cut of cured pork.
explanation.definitionFit: A board game for two players moving counters by dice throws.

clue.text: Terribly rude and thorny, victor under the Lancastrian rose

indicators.note: terribly means badly, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A prickly, rude rose bush, but with a historic victor fighting under that emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The red rose was the Lancastrian badge in the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: He won Bosworth in 1485 as the Lancastrian claimant and became Henry VII.

clue.text: Right to puncture preposterous plan

indicators.note: puncturing goes into something, so one piece enters the other

parts.note: daft means silly, preposterous

explanation.surface: Someone rightly pokes holes in a ridiculous scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A preliminary version of a scheme or document, an outline to be refined.

clue.text: I'm after new setter for the scheduled period

indicators.note: new means remade, so the letters are given a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: Someone chasing a new dog breed for an allotted time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' suggests the dog, but it is the crossword setter, so ME.
explanation.definitionFit: The span of time within which something is planned to happen.

clue.text: Seasick from Barcelona to Marseille? Something eaten for breakfast!

parts.note: sea in Spanish, the language of Barcelona, is mar
sick in French, the language of Marseille, is malade

explanation.surface: A queasy Mediterranean voyage, then breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half of Seasick goes into Spanish, the second into French, matching the journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange preserve spread on toast in the morning.

clue.text: Two pounds into one dime, terribly unlucky

indicators.note: into means one piece goes inside the other
terribly signals the letters are jumbled badly

parts.note: L is an abbreviation for pound, so two pounds give two Ls

explanation.surface: Swapping two pounds for a single dime is a bad deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges the coin's words to IOMENED; L, from the Latin libra, is the usual shorthand for a pound.
explanation.definitionFit: Marked by bad omens, hence doomed or unfortunate.

clue.text: Naturalist without success tours a capital in Khartoum, an African city

indicators.note: touring goes round something, so one piece encloses the other
without means the second piece is removed

parts.note: Charles Darwin was a naturalist
a win is a success

indicators.note: the capital in a word is its initial letter

explanation.surface: A naturalist on a failed trip visits Sudan's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes WIN to leave DAR, and 'tours' puts AK inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Senegal on the West African coast.

clue.text: Something eaten for breakfast — santé?

definitions.meaning: bread dipped in egg and fried, a breakfast dish
the French drinking salute, literally a toast in French

explanation.walkthrough: Santé, meaning health, is what the French say raising a glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg-soaked fried bread, and literally a toast proposed in French.

clue.text: Track, t-track!

parts.note: a rail is a railway track

explanation.walkthrough: The stammer gives T alone, then a rail is a piece of track.
explanation.definitionFit: A path or trail one follows, a synonym of a track.

clue.text: Old leader of the New York Times?

indicators.note: of the places the paper's nationality before its editor

parts.note: the paper is American, so US
the editor, ED, leads a newspaper

explanation.surface: A question about a former head of a famous newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leader' looks like an editorial but is the editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Second-hand goods are no longer new, so old in that sense.

clue.text: Against being held in quarantine

indicators.note: the letters are held inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone is opposed to being kept in isolation.
explanation.definitionFit: A preposition meaning opposed to, as in protesting against a policy.

clue.text: Slowcoach, one with an ice-cream van, did you say?

indicators.note: this phrase signals a word as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: someone at the wheel of an ice-cream van drives sundaes about

explanation.surface: A slow motorist who turns out to be selling ice creams.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone driving slowly and leisurely, as on a weekend outing, holding up traffic.

clue.text: Unfortunately I'm sadder, as now harmless

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone sad at losing their power to hurt.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripped of weapons and so made unable to do harm.

clue.text: See 24
Aboard ship pirate ultimately welcomed — that's funny

indicators.note: being welcomed is being taken in, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: aboard means on
a liner is a passenger ship

indicators.note: ultimately means take the last letter

explanation.surface: A pirate is welcomed onto a ship, which someone finds amusing.
explanation.definitionFit: A short joke delivered in a single sentence.
